worked_solution:
The current $I,$ measured in amperes, is defined as the rate of flow of charge $q,$ measured in coulombs.

$$
I=\frac{dq}{dt}
$$

Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t,$ the differential equation governing the current in the circuit is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{d}{dt}(\frac{dI}{dt}+5I+4q) & =\frac{d}{dt}(11) \\ \frac{{d}^{2}I}{d{t}^{2}}+5\,\frac{dI}{dt}+4\,\frac{dq}{dt} & =0,\end{aligned}
$$

which, when substituting in $I=\frac{dq}{dt},$ gives

$$
\frac{{d}^{2}I}{d{t}^{2}}+5\,\frac{dI}{dt}+4I=0.
$$

The given equation is a second-order linear homogeneous equation with constant coefficients. To find the general solution, we must take a linear combination of two linearly independent solutions.

Assuming the solutions take the form $I={e}^{\lambda t},$ we obtain two solutions, namely, $I={e}^{-4t}$ and $I={e}^{-t}.$
So, the general solution in our case is

$$
I(t)=A{e}^{-4t}+B{e}^{-t}.
$$

We're told that the circuit starts with an initial charge of $\frac{1}{4}\,\text{C}$ on the capacitor and an initial current of $\frac{3}{2}\,\text{A}.$
Now, solving the given relation for $\frac{dI}{dt},$ we have

$$
\frac{dI}{dt}=11-5I-4q.
$$

So, we can apply the initial conditions $I(0)=\frac{3}{2}$ and 

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}^{′}(0) & =11-5I(0)-4q(0) \\  & =11-5\cdot \frac{3}{2}-4\cdot \frac{1}{4} \\  & =\frac{5}{2},\end{aligned}
$$

and solve for $A$ and $B.$

- Substituting $I(0)=\frac{3}{2}$ into our general solution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2} & =A{e}^{-4(0)}+B{e}^{-1(0)} \\ \frac{3}{2} & =A+B.\end{aligned}
$$

- Differentiating $I,$ we get

$$
{I}^{′}=-4A{e}^{-4t}-B{e}^{-t}
$$

Substituting in ${I}^{′}(0)=\frac{5}{2}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{2} & =-4A{e}^{-4(0)}-B{e}^{-1(0)} \\ \frac{5}{2} & =-4A-B.\end{aligned}
$$

Putting the two equations in $A$ and $B$ together gives the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2}=A+B \\ \frac{5}{2}=-4A-B\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system gives $A=-\frac{4}{3}$ and $B=\frac{17}{6}.$ Therefore, the equation for the current (in amperes) in the circuit is

$$
I(t)=-\frac{4}{3}{e}^{-4t}+\frac{17}{6}{e}^{-t}.
$$
